name: Lamar Jackson

background.fact: Born January 7, 1997, in Pompano Beach, Florida; he grew up in the Golden Acres public housing project there.
He played in the same South Florida youth league as future teammate Marquise Brown and, at age 11, won the local youth Super Bowl as quarterback, safety and kicker.
He attended Boynton Beach High School, then played at Louisville, where he won the 2016 Heisman Trophy, Maxwell Award and Walter Camp Award.
Baltimore took him with the last pick of the first round (32nd overall) in the 2018 draft.
He became the starter as a rookie after Joe Flacco was hurt, and was the youngest quarterback to start a playoff game at age 21.
He is a two-time NFL MVP (2019 and 2023) and the all-time leader in quarterback rushing yards.
He is 6 ft 2 in, 205 lb and in his ninth NFL season at age 29.

family.fact: His parents are Felicia Jones and Lamar 'L.J.' Jackson Sr.; his father died of a heart attack in 2005 when Lamar was eight.
He, a younger brother (Jamar) and two younger sisters were raised by their mother, who he says was his first coach and ran hard workouts for him and his brother at age 7.
His brother Jamar played on the same youth team, the Northwest Broward Raiders, that won the title.

recent_events.fact: In Week 4 (a 24-18 home win over Tennessee) he sprained an ankle, then missed Weeks 5 and 6; Ravens went 1-1 in those games.
On November 1 at Buffalo he hurt his right throwing thumb on the first offensive snap when his hand hit pass rusher Greg Rousseau's arm; he watched the second half with a splint.
After the Buffalo loss, coach Jesse Minter said Jackson needed surgery and would go on injured reserve.
Injured reserve means at least four missed games: Jacksonville, the Chargers, Carolina and Houston.
On November 12-13 the team said it was a broken and dislocated thumb with a 6 to 10 week recovery; a surgery was done per ESPN's Jamison Hensley, who projects a return no earlier than Week 16.
ESPN's file lists a return date of 2026-12-27 and describes him as 'doing well'.
Jackson told teammates he plans to return this season; that depends on recovery and presumably whether Baltimore is still in the playoff race.
Minter declined to give details on the injury and said information would 'come from him' (Jackson); outlets called his handling vague.
Baltimore traded with Arizona on November 6 for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who is expected to start while Jackson is out.
Tyler Huntley (toe) and Skylar Thompson are also on injured reserve; the other active quarterbacks are rookie Joe Fagnano and Kedon Slovis.

quotes.fact: Minter after the Buffalo loss on the thumb: 'That'll be a surgery deal. He'll go to (injured reserve).'
Minter's reported answer when asked if the injury could end Jackson's season was one word, 'potentially'.

team_context.fact: Baltimore is 4-5 and fourth in the AFC North after losing four straight (W 41-23 at IND, L 17-24 NO, W 34-31 at DAL, W 24-18 TEN, W 30-23 at ATL OT, L 10-13 at CLE, L 13-35 CIN, L 10-36 at BUF, L 10-33 JAX).
First-year head coach Jesse Minter replaced John Harbaugh (dismissed January 2026); Declan Doyle replaced Todd Monken as offensive coordinator.
AP notes Baltimore averaged 3 fewer yards per play and far fewer points in the games without Jackson than in the three he played (1-2 without him at that point).
Jackson's 2026 line from the data: 5 games, 967 pass yards, 6 TD, 1 INT, 144 rush yards, 15.8 fantasy points a game; Week 4 was a partial game (52 percent of snaps) and Week 8 lasted about one snap.
Zay Flowers is the slot target and Mark Andrews the tight end; Derrick Henry is the lead back whom Baltimore plans to lean on against the Chargers.
Baltimore's defense allowed big games in its last two outings (Jacksonville and Buffalo), per Covers.

next_opponent.fact: Jackson will not play Monday night; the Ravens (BAL -4.5 to -5.5) host the Chargers on ESPN at 8:15 pm ET at M&T Bank Stadium; total 38.5.
Los Angeles is 0-8, last in the AFC West, with its defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary.
The Chargers allowed 4.7 yards per carry over the three games since Week 6 and rank 26th in EPA allowed per handoff over that span.
Chargers safety Derwin James and tackle Rashawn Slater are among those on injured reserve.
Quarterback Justin Herbert left the Houston loss with a non-throwing hand finger injury; X-rays were negative per coach Jim Harbaugh.
Forecast from the data file: clear, 41 F at Baltimore.

style.fact: Widely regarded as the best running quarterback in the NFL, compared with Randall Cunningham and Michael Vick.
Early concerns about being a pure pocket passer faded; most analysts cite improved passing; four perfect passer rating games ties the NFL record.
Madden's week 8 ratings give him 98 overall with 99 throw on the run, 98 under pressure, 98 play action and 96 speed.
Weakness shown this year: durability, with ankle and thumb injuries in 2026; Madden injury rating 92.

availability.detail: Broken and dislocated right thumb, surgery done; 6 to 10 weeks per coach Jesse Minter; ESPN projects earliest return around Week 16, listed date 2026-12-27. Will not play Monday vs LAC.
availability.expected_return: Not before Week 16 (ESPN file lists 2026-12-27); he says he plans to return this season

reasons: He is on injured reserve after thumb surgery with a 6 to 10 week timeline, so the zero is almost certain.
Brissett, acquired November 6, is the expected starter and is described as still learning the playbook.
IR requires at least four missed games and Monday's game is the second of those.
Fantasy value this week is zero regardless of the soft Chargers defense.
